title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: Neighbors influence a person's adoption decision based on the fraction of adopting neighbors and edge weights, compared against the person's social threshold and propensity.

interactions.name: information_broadcast
interactions.description: Information sources broadcast messages that alter perceived risk, norms, or trust, influencing adoption decisions.

interactions.name: policy_effect
interactions.description: Policies (e.g., mandates, campaigns, incentives) modify perceived costs/benefits and norms, increasing or decreasing adoption probability during the policy window.

interactions.name: resource_constraint
interactions.description: Mask supply constraints probabilistically limit adoption even when agents intend to adopt.

interactions.name: risk_signal_update
interactions.description: Exogenous or endogenous risk signals update agents' perceived risk which feeds into adoption decisions.

metrics.name: adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Time series of the proportion of agents wearing masks each day.

metrics.name: final_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Adoption proportion at the end of the simulation horizon.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent_adoption
metrics.description: Number of days until adoption rate first reaches 50%.

metrics.name: peak_adoption_velocity
metrics.description: Maximum day-over-day increase in adoption rate.

metrics.name: retention_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of adopters who remain adopters after a specified period.

metrics.name: switching_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which agents switch from adopt to drop and vice versa.

metrics.name: behavior_reproduction_number
metrics.description: Average number of new adoptions directly attributable to a newly adopting agent during early diffusion.

metrics.name: policy_impact
metrics.description: Difference in adoption metrics with vs. without a policy (e.g., final adoption rate delta or area under adoption curve).

metrics.name: influence_inequality
metrics.description: Gini coefficient of the distribution of adoptions attributed to individual influencers.

metrics.name: assortativity_by_adoption
metrics.description: Network assortativity coefficient w.r.t. adoption state (homophily of adopters).
